sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling from one fixed strictly positive compatible observed law \(p\).
sampling_model.treatment: The macro intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X=c_x)\) is the causal query and is not randomly assigned in the observational sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cell is positive; regular-stratum inference imposes the fixed margin \(\min_a p(a)\ge\eta\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is required: \(\widehat p_N\) is the empirical complete-cell law, circuit derivatives are obtained by arithmetic-DAG differentiation on \(\mathcal U\), the plug-in estimator uses a fixed uniform target vector and zero covariance outside \(\mathcal U\), and boundary inference propagates \(R_N\) through every certified guard.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 6 states that the ID algorithm is sound and complete for macro effects in an acyclic C-DAG.
Theorem 4 states that failure of one cluster do-calculus rule has a compatible ADMG witness under its cluster-size condition.
The ID algorithm returns an observational expression or a hedge and is complete for one fixed recursive semi-Markovian graph.
Equivalent single conditional-interventional kernels in one ADMG admit a canonical derivation using at most four do-calculus rule applications.
Theorem 2 gives a sufficient graphical criterion for one causal effect to share an identifying formula across candidate SA-MPDAGs.
For functional causal structures with two binary observed variables, algebraic elimination yields feasibility tests and can recover identifiable causal parameters.
Algorithm IDP identifies effects uniformly over one PAG-represented Markov equivalence class whenever its recursive criterion succeeds.
The public manuscript claims that three representatives per cluster preserve macro identifiability and that the resulting procedure is atomically complete.

body.tldr: A known arbitrary clustering of an acyclic micro causal system can create a cyclic macro diagram and a union of observational model images. The proposal characterizes uniform macro-effect identification by local ID plus agreement on every common-law overlap, then asks for a constructive ranked saturation required to preserve guard coverage, local values, and all pairwise comparison cells until it emits one common-value guarded circuit or two bounded positive finite SCMs with the same complete observed law and different macro effects. An affirmative construction yields Global-CID and, conditionally on its size analysis, the displayed elementary bound; total branchwise multinomial inference uses a harmless fallback outside its local extension neighborhood, while a simultaneous region remains valid at guard boundaries.

project_justification.gap: Published C-DAG completeness covers acyclic cluster diagrams, and recent cyclic C-DMG results prove soundness or rulewise completeness but explicitly do not reconcile different derivations across compatible refinements or furnish a complete common-law collision converse.
project_justification.niche: Finite alphabets and known memberships make the arbitrary-cluster model a finite union of recursive ADMG images, so the unresolved mathematical object is an overlap-sensitive symbolic normal form rather than another local do-calculus rule.
project_justification.fill: Global-CID combines ordinary ID within each exact refinement with a ranked fixing-overlap saturation satisfying explicit coverage and value-preservation invariants, emitting either one common-value guarded functional valid on the entire union or a bounded pair of legal positive SCMs that certifies failure. Its elementary bound is conditional on constructing and sizing that saturation, and its circuit feeds a total regular-stratum estimator and boundary-robust inference.

body.related_work: ShpitserPearl2006JointID, Theorems 4, 6, and 7, establishes the formula-or-hedge standard for one fixed ADMG and supplies the local recursive engine. AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG, Theorems 5 and 6, lifts do-calculus and ID to acyclic cluster diagrams but excludes cyclic quotients. FerreiraAssaad2025CDMGADMG, Theorem 4 and its conclusion, treats cyclic cluster quotients but explicitly limits completeness to individual rule failures and leaves different successful rule sequences and a complete nonidentification criterion unresolved. TehSadeghiSoo2025RobustID, Theorem 2, motivates robustness across non-equivalent graph candidates but provides a sufficient common-expression criterion on SA-MPDAGs rather than an overlap-sensitive if-and-only-if result. JaberZhangBareinboim2019PAGID handles a single PAG equivalence class whose members share one statistical model, unlike the union of refinement-specific observable images here. TikkaHelskeKarvanen2023TransitClusters proves preservation for a restricted contraction class and demonstrates why arbitrary clustering is not benign. LeeSpekkens2017AlgebraicCausal shows that semialgebraic elimination can characterize tiny finite functional structures; it is used only as a certificate checker, not as the identification algorithm. YvernesEtAl2026DerivationGraphs gives a four-step normal form for individual interventional kernels in one ADMG and identifies finite normal forms for complete ID expressions as open. ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCF supplies fixed-graph finite canonical SCMs, while the proposed bounded collision theorem adds paired exact-refinement activity, positivity, and complete-law equality. BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022Semiparametric and FangSantos2019DirectionalInference inform the smooth-branch and nonregular-boundary inference layers after graphical identification is settled.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The ordinary finite-union equivalence is semantic and does not itself provide a guarded circuit. Raw rational comparison is unsound because two formulas may differ on the free simplex yet agree on the intersection of their refinement images. Conversely, separately constructed hedge witnesses need not share one observed law, and the union of acyclic witness refinements may contain a directed cycle. The ranked fixing-overlap normal form must preserve its guard-cover, local-value, exact-unresolved-pair, and no-lost-disagreement invariant until it produces the fully encoded positive or negative terminal certificate. Generic real quantifier elimination may check a terminal algebraic certificate but does not count as Global-CID, and the \(E_4\) bound is not asserted without the missing decreasing-rank construction and size analysis.
body.honest_scope: The semantic gluing criterion, finite refinement enumeration, bounded-support compression architecture, and multinomial inference reductions have direct proof routes. The constructive overlap normal form remains open: its saturation invariant and terminal encodings are specified, but a decreasing rank, branch coverage proof, exact witness extraction, and size analysis must still be supplied. The \(B_{\mathrm{out}}(\ell)\) complexity and output bound is conditional on that construction. The result concerns complete macro interventions on known clusters in finite recursive semi-Markovian SCMs with exact graph activity and positive observed laws; it does not identify micro interventions, cyclic micro-SCM effects, or clinical efficacy. On acyclic C-DAGs and singleton partitions it must reduce to the published cluster-ID and ordinary-ID results.
